entities.name: PMID:27499636
observations: Wang et al. studied AG490 combined with DC-activated AFP-specific T cells against HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells.
The combination enhanced in-vitro antitumor activity and was interpreted as Fas/FasL-signal independent; mechanistic independence was not tested by Fas/FasL blockade.

entities.name: AG490
observations: AG490, a JAK2 inhibitor, was combined with DC-activated AFP-specific CD8-positive T cells in the HepG2 model.

entities.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
observations: The study used HepG2 hepatocellular-carcinoma cells as the tumor model.

entities.name: HepG2
observations: HepG2 cells were treated or cocultured with AG490 and DC-activated AFP-specific T cells.

entities.name: AG490 combination enhancement
observations: In vitro, AG490 plus AFP-specific T cells reduced HepG2 viability, increased apoptosis, induced G1 arrest, and produced the highest reported IL-2, IL-6, IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha, perforin, and granzyme B levels versus T cells alone.

entities.name: Fas/FasL independence interpretation
observations: Treatment reportedly did not change tumor-cell Fas or FasL expression, while BAX increased; perforin and granzyme B increased. The paper therefore interpreted the effect as Fas/FasL-signal independent, but no anti-Fas/anti-FasL blockade or neutralization rescue experiment was identified.
